comments.body:
Reproduction (before the fix), 2026-10-31, macOS host, Python 3.12.14, worktree at 66be683cc7c. Method: a scratch pytest plugin wraps one function inside each test's timed window and, when it is called, a helper sends SIGSTOP to the whole test process and SIGCONT after N seconds (models a descheduled CI worker). Without the plugin the 3 tests pass (3 passed in 3.79s).
- test_doctor_mapping: freeze 4.5 s at entry to doctor_mapping._run_bounded -> 3 of 3 failed: "AssertionError: doctor must not block on a hanging probe" (elapsed >= 4.0). Note: a freeze inside the probe worker thread did not land inside the window reliably (helper spawn outlasted the 0.2 s join), so the entry point is used.
- test_review_bot lifespan: freeze 2.5 s, scheduled 0.1 s after shutdown_cancel_seconds() is called (inside the 0.3 s cancel window) -> 3 of 3 failed: "review-bot shutdown took 2.74s / 2.75s / 2.85s".
- test_gate_admission_09da refusal: freeze 5.5 s inside the 2nd _acquire_slot call (the refused admission) -> 3 of 3 failed: "admission blocked for 5.58s / 5.55s / 5.56s instead of fast-failing".
Observation for the gate test: removing LOCK_NB (the real defect) makes the same-process second flock block forever, so the 5 s ceiling never evaluates; only pytest-timeout (300 s) would end it. The ceiling therefore catches stalls, not the queueing defect.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
cuddly-callous-antlion (fixed in 844dd26b854) showed CI unit workers stall for seconds: the py3.11 job spent 4.78 s in a test whose work takes 0.3 s, and the same run took 1.751 s in a fixture that only sets environment variables. Three other "hang-guard" tests assert a wall-clock ceiling whose margin is smaller than or close to stalls of that size:
- `tests/unit/test_doctor_mapping.py:315`: `elapsed < 4.0` against a probe that sleeps 5.0 s; a 4 s stall fails it, and the margin over the 5 s failure mode is 1 s.
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:2311`: `elapsed < 2.0` for a lifespan shutdown; a 2 s stall fails it.
- `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py:168`: `elapsed < 5.0` for a refusal that takes microseconds; a 5 s stall fails it.

Freezing the whole test process (SIGSTOP/SIGCONT from a helper, triggered by a scratch pytest plugin when a function inside the timed window is called) past each ceiling fails all 3 tests in 3 of 3 runs (evidence in comments).

## Expected
Each test proves its property (the hang was abandoned, the shutdown was bounded, the refusal did not queue) by an ordering or state observation that a descheduled test process cannot break, as 844dd26b854 did for test_llm_timeouts.py.

## Plan
Test-only change; no production code changes. Each wall-clock assert and its `# timing: hang-guard` marker is removed together (the wall-clock-assert lint only fires on an upper-bound assert, so no marker is needed once the assert is gone).
1. `test_degradation_slow_probe_times_out_to_unavailable`: the fake probe parks on a `threading.Event` (bounded 30 s wait so the thread always exits) instead of `time.sleep(5.0)`, and sets a `probe_finished` flag when it leaves. After `scan_mapping` returns, assert the probe has NOT finished (it is still parked, so doctor returned without waiting for it) and the single `unavailable` finding's reason names the timeout; release the probe in `finally`. Defect check: `thread.join(timeout)` -> `thread.join()` in `_run_bounded` makes the probe finish before return, so the test fails.
2. `test_lifespan_cancel_await_is_bounded_for_a_task_slow_to_cancel`: the slow reconciler swallows the first cancel, then sleeps a bounded 30 s and records `finished_on_its_own` if not cancelled again; a second cancel is recorded and honored. Drop the outer `wait_for(..., 10)` safety net and the elapsed assert; assert 2 cancels were delivered and the task did not finish on its own, i.e. lifespan's own `shutdown_cancel_seconds` bound cancelled it. Defect check: replacing the bounded `wait_for(gather(...))` in `lifespan` with a bare `await gather(...)` makes the task finish on its own after 1 cancel, so the test fails (after ~30 s, not a hang).
3. `test_the_refusal_returns_immediately_rather_than_waiting_for_a_holder`: after t-1 has been admitted (inside its `with`), and immediately before the t-2 attempt, replace `ga.fcntl` with a proxy whose `flock` records each call's flags and delegates, so t-1's own acquire is never in the record. Restore the real module right after the refusal (before t-1's release runs). Assert the refused t-2 admission made exactly `limit` (1) lock attempts, each with `LOCK_NB`, i.e. it never asked to wait and never polled. A spy call without `LOCK_NB` fails the test immediately rather than deadlocking. Defect checks: dropping `LOCK_NB` in `_open_slot`, and a retry loop around `_acquire_slot`, each make the test fail.
4. Re-run each test 3 times under the same freeze; run the 3 test files, `make lint` (including the wall-clock-assert gate), `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of the 3 tests passes 3 of 3 runs under a pause longer than its former ceiling.
- [ ] Re-introducing each test's defect makes that test fail.
- [ ] make lint exits 0.
- [ ] make typecheck exits 0.
- [ ] The change merges with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

## File impact (expected)
- tests/unit/test_doctor_mapping.py
- tests/unit/test_review_bot.py
- tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py
